implementation_notes: Spring Integration names the pattern: ContentEnricher (XML <int:enricher>, DSL .enrich(...)) sends the message - or the subset selected by request-payload-expression - to a request channel, receives the resource reply and merges it into the original payload through property expressions; should-clone-payload decides whether the inbound instance is mutated. Spring Integration 6 follows the Spring Framework 6 Java 17+ baseline. Choose it when the enrichment is one declared step of a flow: the framework owns request/reply, correlation, timeout and the merge.
pitfalls: Without a request-channel the enricher can only add static values or expressions over the original message - it silently never calls the resource.
The enricher blocks on the reply (send-timeout applies); a slow resource backs up the flow unless the lookup runs on its own executor behind a circuit breaker.
should-clone-payload=false mutates the inbound message instance, so other references can observe half-enriched payloads.

variants.name: Apache Camel enrich / pollEnrich route step
variants.implementation_notes: Camel implements the EIP directly: .enrich('http:...') obtains a resource exchange through a producer and combines it with the original exchange via an AggregationStrategy, while .pollEnrich uses a polling consumer (file, FTP) for the same job; without a strategy Camel simply replaces the outgoing message with the resource reply. Dynamic URIs (.enrich().simple("http:myserver/${header.orderId}/order")) make the endpoint depend on message content, cacheSize caches and reuses producers, and aggregateOnException decides whether a failed lookup still reaches the strategy. Use it when the integration already lives in a Camel route.
pitfalls: Omitting the AggregationStrategy silently discards the original message: Camel uses the resource reply as the result exchange.
The resource exchange has its own unit of work unless shareUnitOfWork=true, so rolling back the main exchange does not roll back the enrichment call.
Dynamic enrich URIs built from message content need an allowed-schemes allow-list, or a crafted message steers the enricher at an unintended endpoint.

variants.name: Function<Order,Order> over a lookup cache
variants.implementation_notes: Outside an integration framework the pattern is a function: read the key, resolve the record once (cache-aside with ConcurrentHashMap.computeIfAbsent or Caffeine), merge it into the message and return it. The enricher becomes a composable Function<Order,Order> that chains with other transformations, and the resource call is wrapped in a CompletableFuture with a timeout so a slow system degrades instead of blocking the consumer thread. Choose it for small services that must not pull in an integration stack.
pitfalls: computeIfAbsent runs the mapping function while holding a bin lock, so one slow lookup blocks unrelated keys hashing to the same bin.
Caching Customer.unknown(id) forever turns a transient outage into permanent missing data - cache negatives only with a TTL.
Exceptions from the mapping function escape computeIfAbsent; 'resource unavailable' and 'not found' need separate handling.
